subject: computer-science

moments.title: Agile Manifesto
moments.body: In February 2001, 17 developers — including Kent Beck (Extreme Programming), Martin Fowler, Ward Cunningham, Robert Martin, Jeff Sutherland and Ken Schwaber (Scrum) — meet at a ski resort and produce the Agile Manifesto: four values, twelve principles. 'Individuals and interactions over processes and tools.'
moments.takeaway: A short document by 17 people defined how the global software industry organises work for the next 25 years.

now.title: Software process today
now.body: Agile, Scrum, Kanban and SAFe are standard in most software organisations. The original signatories have mostly become critics of how Agile has been implemented — particularly large enterprise frameworks. DevOps (2009), continuous deployment, and SRE practices (Google, 2003) extended the same ideas to operations.
now.open_questions: Did Agile improve software outcomes or just speed up bad software? Empirical evidence is mixed.

reflection: The Manifesto's signatories had vastly different practices. They agreed on values rather than methodology. Most subsequent debate has confused the two.
